newsitem.title: USA: UN approves two Iraqi crude contracts, total at 33.
newsitem.headline: UN approves two Iraqi crude contracts, total at 33.

text.p: United Nations overseers have approved two more Iraqi crude contracts, bringing the total number to 33 ratified since the start of the oil-for-food accord on December 10, U.N. officials said Monday.
Room has been created under the limited oil deal's dollar cap since world oil prices started to tumble in recent weeks, thus producing the additional approvals.
"The overseers are discussing adding one or two more spot contracts since oil prices have been lower," added a U.N. official.
Overseers are charged with approving $1 billion worth of contracts for each 90-day period of the accord. The first 90-day period will expire March 9.

Under the oil deal, Iraq is allowed to sell a total of $2 billion worth of crude over the six months, in order to buy aid for civilians suffering from sanctions slapped on Baghdad after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
In addition, the U.N. official said the sanctions committee on Iraq has not scheduled a formal meeting this week, and will meet only a consultative basis.
Last Friday, the sanctions panel met and discussed possible technical changes to the way it approves aid contracts, with the goal of speeding-up food and supply imports to Iraq.
